newsitem.title: USA: Morrow sees Q4 sales off expectations.
newsitem.headline: Morrow sees Q4 sales off expectations.

text.p: Morrow Snowboards Inc, a maker of premium snowboards and related products, said on Friday fourth quarter sales will be about even with 1995's $9.6 million, which is lower than it had expected.
Sales for the full year are expected to range between $30 and $32 million, about 30 percent above 1995.

"Our products appear to be selling through well at the retail level," Chief Executive Officer David Calapp said in a statement. "(But) there appears to be an oversupply of boards from other manufacturers, and this has affected our level of reorders."
Through the first nine months of the year, Morrow reported net income of $0.28 a share on revenue of $22.3 million.
Analysts had forecast earnings of $0.52 a share for the full year and $0.24 a share for the fourth quarter, according to First Call.

Morrow said because of the oversupply of snowboards, some retailers are reluctant to order additional Morrow product even though they are selling well. Also, other manufacturers are offering substantial discounts to clear inventory.
In California, a key market for for Morrow with about 40 percent of U.S. sales, snow has fallen later than expected.
Morrow entered the fourth quarter with over $7 million in backlog, it said. And history indicates it could have expected to receive $4 to $7 million more orders in the fourth quarter.
"It now appears that net fourth quarter reorders will be below that level," Morrow said.
